title: Sealed baseline: classify a failing suite against the starting files (EVD-04, slice 1)
body:
## What

EVD-04, slice 1 (sealed baseline), from the local spec `sealed-baseline.md` §15.1 and §15.3. Slice 2 (committed-tree check) stays cut. Built under the owner's "finish the untested Musts fast" direction: no feature-spec review or sign-off for this build.

When the broader suite (`OB-suite`) still fails after flaky reruns on a full candidate check, `check` runs the same test command once more in the same call, on a copy of the contract's starting files outside the workspace, and classifies the failure:

- **pre-existing** (fails at the start with the same file, test, kind and first-line message signature, and both lists are complete): `baseline-failure-not-excluded` blocks and the `baseline-failures` question (exit 3) asks the user; no attempt and no failure signature are recorded.
- **introduced** (absent from a complete starting record, or in a test file that did not exist at the start, which needs no run): stays `evidence-failed`, now worded "weren't failing this way on a run of your starting files" / "new tests that fail"; `finish` still demands another attempt.
- **changed** (fails at both, differently) or **unknown** (with the reason): `classification-unknown` blocks and the same question asks.

`decide baseline-failures`: `exclude` needs the user's words as `--quote` and records an exception (TS §8.1 shape; note `baseline-failure-excluded`, or the new `baseline-failure-unclassified-excluded` for an unknown one); `fix` makes the failures this work's to fix (`evidence-failed`). A failure left out counts as passed for the review manifest and `commit`'s checkpoint, and costs no attempt. A later check reuses the record without a second sealed run.

The copy is written from Git's object store (`ls-tree -r --long` plus one `cat-file --batch`): no checkout, no index, no filter, no hook, nothing written to the repository; it is deleted when the run ends.

## Simplifications (disclosed; also in `CHANGELOG.md`)

- **Dependencies:** the workspace's `node_modules` is linked into the copy only when the starting `package.json` and lockfile equal the current files, a lockfile exists, `package.json` has no `workspaces`, and no top-level package links into the workspace. Otherwise the result is unknown with `sealed-deps-unavailable`. No other dependency sharing.
- **Refusals instead of programs:** any configured Git filter that applies here (the existing filter gate), a submodule, a tracked symbolic link, a symlinked or read-excluded start-dirty file, a start tree over 50,000 files or 500 MB, or a start-dirty file changed since `open` makes the result unknown without running anything. Materialization errors are not retried.
- **Bounds:** 200 failure ids per list (more is unknown). A suite whose first run took over 2 minutes is not run again (unknown). A timed-out, killed, invalid or concurrently-edited starting run is retried once at a later check.
- **No sealed receipt:** only the record is kept, so SB-12's `candidateReceipts` reader change was not needed.
- **No adapter version bump (SB-13):** receipts from before this change have no `failureIds`, are not classified, and keep the old `evidence-failed` reading.
- **Excluded unknown** also counts as passed for the review gate (the spec says this only for pre-existing); its note says it was not shown to fail before.
- **Skill text:** none names the new decision; the question's options say how to answer.
- Signatures blank paths and digits in the first message line; ignored or generated files are absent from the copy (a disclosed limit the signature mitigates, not removes).

## Evidence

- Local (Windows): `npm run typecheck`, `lint-arch`, `lint-skills`, `lint-quality` pass. `coverage --milestone R1` lists EVD-04 as mapped; it still exits 1 for other sessions' unmapped Musts (AGT-10, GIT-09, CON-07, QLT-05, QLT-11, QLT-13, NFR-07). `npm run privacy` clean.
- Pure tests (`baseline.test.ts`, 10, incl. a `fast-check` property that nothing is pre-existing without complete lists; `verdict.test.ts`, 67) and the materializer test (E12) pass locally.
- `sealed-baseline.test.ts` E1, E2, E3, E4, E10 drive real Git and Vitest through `open`, `check`, `decide`, `finish`; mutating work is refused on Windows, so they run only in the `untrusted` CI on Ubuntu and macOS.
- Not covered by a test: E5–E7 are pure only; E8 (fault at materialize, filter), E9 transient retry, E11 concurrent edit, E13, E14 (kill during the sealed run) have no test. macOS temp-path behaviour is exercised only by CI. Unobserved on the real host.

Do not merge without the owner's "Merge it".
